newsitem.title: FRANCE: French parliament approves TV blackout sanction.
newsitem.headline: French parliament approves TV blackout sanction.

text.p: France's National Assembly approved legislation on Thursday allowing the nation's broadcast watchdog to impose five to 10 minute blackouts on programmes breaching rules limiting sex, violence or foreign programmes.

The amendment, proposed by two parliamentarians of the centrist UDF, the junior partner in the ruling coalition, was adopted against the advice of Culture Minister Philippe Douste Blazy who had likened the television blackouts to the "atomic bomb".

Parliamentarians Laurent Dominati and Alain Griotteray, who penned the amendment, argued that the Higher Audiovisual Council (CSA) had "hardly any other means of inflicting truly dissuasive punishment on violators".
The CSA has imposed quotas on French films and other programmes to protect the television industry from mainly U.S. imports.

"The interruption of a programme for limited period, at an important time slot, could have for the broadcaster in question a highly dissuasive effect that goes beyond the financial consequences..," they said in their arguments.
The government still hopes to defeat the amendment when it goes to the Senate for approval or in a second vote by the National Assembly.
